identity.issuer: Cascade Specialty Chemicals, LLC (internal record; header on page 1)
identity.site: Portland — 4410 NW Front Ave, Portland, Oregon 97210

scan.summary: This is your own daily pre-shift checklist for forklift FL-2 for September 2026. It is a photo, and the bottom is cut off. A log like this shows that the truck was checked before each shift and that defects were acted on. It is judged on whether it is complete and up to date. The visible part runs from Sep 1 to Sep 17. It is missing two working days, and it records a horn defect with no record of a repair or of the truck being taken out of service.
scan.freshness_note: The last visible entry is Sep 17, 2026, which is 10 days before today (2026-09-27). The photo is cropped at the bottom edge, so later rows may exist and simply not be in the picture. Ask for a full, uncropped scan of the sheet so that it covers Sep 18 through today.

gaps.title: Horn defect Sep 9 with no repair or out-of-service record
gaps.description: On Sep 9 the horn is marked X with the note 'Horn not working'. The next day it is ticked OK, but nothing records a repair, who did it, or that the truck was taken out of service. The hour meter goes from 4,847 on Sep 9 to 4,853 on Sep 10. That suggests (inferred) that about 6 hours of use happened after the defect was found.
gaps.fix: Find out whether the horn was repaired and when. Add a dated repair or out-of-service note to the log, signed by whoever made the repair, or attach the work order. Going forward, add a 'defect reported to / repaired on / returned to service by' field to the sheet, and tag the truck out of service until a safety defect is fixed.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) and 1910.178(p)(1), adopted by reference in Oregon under OAR 437-002-0220
gaps.locator: Page 1, Sep 9 row (Horn column and Notes)

gaps.title: No inspection recorded Sep 3 and Sep 4
gaps.description: The log jumps from Sep 2 to Sep 7. Sep 3 and 4 were a Thursday and Friday (inferred from the calendar). The hour meter goes from 4,819 on Sep 2 to 4,834 on Sep 7. That is about 15 hours, or roughly two days of use at this truck's usual 6–7 hours a day, so the truck appears to have been operated without a recorded pre-shift check (inferred).
gaps.fix: Confirm whether FL-2 was used on Sep 3 and 4. If it was, record what happened and remind operators that the check comes before every shift the truck is used. If a separate sheet exists for those days, file it with this log. Do not backfill entries.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7), adopted by reference in Oregon under OAR 437-002-0220
gaps.locator: Page 1, between the Sep 2 and Sep 7 rows

gaps.title: Entries after Sep 17 not visible
gaps.description: The photo ends at the Sep 17 row and the bottom edge is cut off. Any entries for Sep 18–27 are either missing from the log or missing from the image.
gaps.fix: Rescan the whole sheet flat and uncropped. If there are no entries after Sep 17, find out whether the truck was used and why it was not checked.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7), adopted by reference in Oregon under OAR 437-002-0220
gaps.locator: Page 1, bottom of the table (image cut off)

deadlines.title: Pre-shift inspection of forklift FL-2 before each shift it is used
deadlines.source_line: Inspection per OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7): examine before each shift; do not use if a defect affects safety.

facts.value: Toyota 8FGU25 forklift, unit FL-2, propane-fuelled, at the Portland warehouse
facts.affects: Brings in the forklift inspection, operator training and LPG handling rules at the Portland site.

facts.value: The propane tank on FL-2 was changed on site on Sep 15, 2026
facts.affects: On-site LPG cylinder changes and storage bring in propane handling, storage and fire code requirements.

facts.value: Only day-shift entries appear for FL-2 in September. This may mean the truck runs one shift, but it cannot be confirmed from this log.
facts.affects: If the site ran round the clock, the check would be needed after each shift, not just daily.

facts.value: At least two people operate FL-2, identified only by the initials M.C. and J.R. Their certification cannot be confirmed from this log.
facts.affects: Each operator needs training and evaluation records under 1910.178(l).
